speaker: Doctor
text: What specific antibiotic were you prescribed and for what condition? Also, how many days after starting the medication did the rash and joint pain begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction (also known as delayed-type hypersensitivity to beta-lactams).

The rash starting in the antecubital and popliteal fossae spreading to the trunk one week after starting amoxicillin for sinusitis, accompanied by fever and arthralgia, is classic for this diagnosis. I do not need further tests to confirm this clinical picture.
